in_hebrew.name: יוֹשֻע
in_hebrew.long_meaning: יוֹשֻע, (Yōšūă') - 'salvation is of the Lord', 'Yahweh is salvation', or 'Yah is deliverance'. In Hebrew, the name means 'God is salvation' or 'YHWH is deliverance'. In the Hebrew Bible, Joshua (Yehoshua) is the name of the leader who succeeded Moses, leading the Israelites into the Promised Land (Numbers 27:18-23, Deuteronomy 31:1-23, 34:9). The name has its roots in the Hebrew words 'YHVH' (God) and 'Yasha' (save, deliver). Historically, the name has been used in Jewish tradition to signify God's salvation and deliverance. In Christian tradition, the name Joshua (Yōšūă') has been adopted to signify God's salvation through Jesus Christ, highlighting His deliverance and salvation of humanity.

in_greek.name: Ιώσηρος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ιώσηρος, (Iṓsēros) - 'σωτήριος', (sōtēríos) - 'deliverer', 'savior', or 'rescuer'. In Greek, the name Iosēros is derived from the verb 'σώζειν' (sōzein), meaning 'to save' or 'to deliver'. In the New Testament, the name Jesus (Ἰησοῦς, Iēsoûs) is the Greek form of the Hebrew name Joshua (יוֹשֻע, Yōšūă'). The name has its roots in the Greek words 'σώζειν' and 'θεός' (theos), meaning 'God'. Historically, the name has been used in early Christian tradition to signify Jesus Christ as the savior and deliverer of humanity.

in_latin.name: Josue
in_latin.long_meaning: Josue, -i (gen.), -e (dat.), -em (acc.) - 'salvator', 'liberator', or 'rescuer'. In Latin, the name Josue is derived from the verb 'salvare', meaning 'to save' or 'to deliver'. In Christian tradition, the name Josue has been used to signify Jesus Christ as the savior and deliverer of humanity. Historically, the name has been used in early Christian tradition to emphasize God's salvation and deliverance of humanity through Jesus Christ.
